name: Charcoal Drawing / Pastel (Drawing and Illustration; supplemental provenance, not a directly named source style).
visualIdentity: Charcoal and pastel are separate dry-media techniques, and the primary medium must be chosen. Charcoal emphasizes tonal mass, hatching, and smudging. Pastel shows softly layered pigment with visible grain. Preserve paper texture and localized powder edges while revealing or erasing marks. Avoid uniform noise that obscures structure.
suitableUses: Source explicitly states that charcoal or pastel works best alone for tonal drawings. Source does not list specific use cases. Inferred suitability: tonal illustration, figure studies, and atmospheric or mood-driven pieces where marks are revealed or erased, though this is not stated in the source.
limitations: Source-stated limits: do not conflate charcoal and pastel, do not add uniform noise that hides structure, and do not use per-frame random grain. Hybrids must avoid invented footage and photo detail retention. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production. Pastel colors must come from a pastel reference. Duration, aspect ratio, resolution, and frame rate are unspecified.
palette: The palette is an authored, unsupplied example: background #EDE7DC and foreground #353330, monochrome, with gradients disabled. Foreground on background measures 10.233 contrast, which meets the 4.5 normal-text target on a two-color basis only. Task-supplied exact colors override this. Do not add accent hues; express tone through hatching or opacity. Verify contrast on composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: The source gives no style-specific motion direction. Shared guidance favors smooth authored movement while preserving deliberate cuts, impacts, and reading holds. Mark reveals and erasures should be handled locally with masks and derived from composition time. Optional motion patterns 012 (chaptered handoff) and 015 (narrative storytelling) apply only when the scene supports them, and choosing neither is valid. Interactivity applies only to interactive delivery, not video.
audio: Audio direction is unspecified for this style. Source offers only suggestion dimensions: music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, with no fixed genre, tempo, or voice. Inferred: restrained or silent audio suits drawn reveals and reading holds. Audio must not compete with narration. User audio requirements take priority, and no audio assets are supplied.
assetRequirements: No assets are supplied, so requirements are unspecified. The style needs fixed grain brushes, smudge masks, and paper layers. Charcoal values and pastel color layers are built separately. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Optional Python and Pillow support preprocessing and masks. Hybrid style-090 requires supplied footage; none should be invented.
combinations: Source suggests charcoal or pastel works best alone for tonal drawings. Hybrids help when figure motion needs reference footage or atmospheric depth. Style-090 provides rotoscoped figure motion, requires supplied footage, and keeps charcoal palette only with fixed grain per frame. Style-101 adds atmospheric depth layers with grain anchored to paper and limited movement. Avoid moving paper texture and added colors.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default composition and export pipeline. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and that reason must be recorded. Canvas 2D is the style renderer for brushes, textures, and masks. The motion engine is unspecified for this style and should be chosen per action, with one owner per animated property. Delivery requires inspecting key frames, watching the video, and checking audio sync and loop continuity.
